title: Most Events & Plugins in a Single Game?

posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body: I was curious to see how many events & plugins someone has successfully crammed into a single game (tutorial, demo, or completed)? It doesn't matter which version of RPG Maker.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body: I don't really see the point of this question, since the amount of events/plugins has no impact on the performance of the game if done correctly, but I'm sitting at about 160 plugins right now. Haven't counted my events.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body: I also think I've seen a couple people load ALL the Yanfly plugins in a single project so that's around 200

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
I'm at 52 plugins, but without any further information about their purpose, you can't really tell, if they have any impact on performance or something. Some might change a single parameter or add one line of code, others might contain complex, calculation heavy features.
I don't know how to count events spread all over the game. I guess something like 8000? In terms of common events, there are ~650 in my project. Still, numbers per se won't give a clue about being "successfully crammed" or not.

posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body:
SGHarlekin said:

Click to expand...
Overall, just doing some stress testing.
I'll explain, I did some analytics and the best platforms to release for were mobile (Apple and Google) and Steam (
Statista video game industry - Statistics & Facts
). Mobile seems to be the bottleneck in performance for most situations, but in other cases I'm wondering about technical limitations in different RPG Makers. When I did web development, I had a kit something like this.
I've had a lot of phones that were unable to render anything 3D unless I used emulated 3D. I can get Babylon.js or Three.js to render, but the performance is subpar on some devices. Not unplayable, but if I threw in 200-1000 plugins, I'm wondering if low-end users could play it? Or if they have an issue, how could I troubleshoot it?
When developing on the PC, it has the best versatility, but customers can have very unusual system configurations. The best I can do to try and fix bugs is run it through a VM with Oracle Virtualbox.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body: The absolute number of plugins isn't a good indicator because not all plugins are created equal. Things like rendering 3D, lighting and pathfinding are going to be more performance intensive than a plugin that just lets you change the formatting of a menu.

posts.author: ZimXero
posts.body:
What Aqua said.
Some plugins are tiny memory, some are large.
Some plugins are resource intensive, some are not.
A lot of plugins are essentially dormant, and just allow or redirect something minor.
The biggest hit on performance is Common Events, but again... it's how they are used or misused.  A few common events could cause lag if they are forcing constant evaluations and rechecks involving large searches or calculations.  A game could have a thousand common events and run on mobile just fine, if they are considerate of resource management.
I've heard that the second biggest potential hit on performance is memory leakage... not easily controllable without a lot of knowledge and testing.
To reduce resource drain, limit common events and use them smartly, limit your plugins to the ones that actually matter, keep your map sizes down to what your story needs, and remove unused files from your projects.
Mobile platform has some incredibly in-depth games... RPG maker is not a limiting factor.
